advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/limit the substring-atom oracle's evasion surface (import aliasing, non-literal relation names) or strengthen it toward an AST/definition-count check so a re-implementation cannot hide by spelling the atoms differently.
evidence: 273:        if not all(atom in text for atom in _WALK_ATOMS):

close_disposition.py:139-140 shows the relation is compared to the literal string "supersedes"; a copy comparing to a module constant (e.g. types.py enumerates "supersedes" among relations) would not carry the literal and would slip past.
advisory.finding: The guard's oracle is a verbatim substring conjunction ('find_inbound_relationships(' AND '"supersedes"'). A genuine second walk that aliases the import (e.g. `from rebar.reducer._inbound import find_inbound_relationships as fir` then `fir(...)`, or builds the relation name via a variable/constant instead of the literal `"supersedes"`) evades detection, so an empty offenders list cannot distinguish 'no re-implementation exists' from 'a re-implementation exists but does not spell both atoms literally'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify (or relax) the escape rule so a reasoned marker adjacent to a multi-line walk is honoured, matching the documented per-walk escape intent.
evidence: 277:            if not any(atom in line for atom in _WALK_ATOMS):
260:    A legitimate second walk escapes with ``# replacement-walk-ok: <why>`` on one of the lines
ABSENCE: the marker must be inline on an atom-bearing line; there is no allowance for the marker on a preceding/following comment line, which is where a multi-line rationale would typically live.
advisory.finding: The excused-detection loop only accepts a '# replacement-walk-ok:' marker when it sits on a line that itself contains one of the atoms; a legitimate multi-line second walk (atoms on separate lines) whose reasoned marker is placed on an adjacent comment line — the natural place to explain the block — is still reported as an offender, contradicting the docstring's framing of a per-'walk' escape.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives `_replacement_walk_offenders` (or a parameterized helper) against synthetic file contents proving it FLAGS an unmarked duplicate, EXCUSES one with a reasoned `# replacement-walk-ok: <why>` marker, and REJECTS a bare reasonless marker — encoding the mutation proof the commit message describes.
evidence: `_replacement_walk_offenders` is invoked only at lines 297 and 300, both inside the same `== []` assertion; no test constructs a synthetic module containing both atoms to prove the function actually FLAGS it, nor one carrying `# replacement-walk-ok: <reason>` to prove excusal works, nor a bare `# replacement-walk-ok:` to prove a reasonless marker is rejected.

The commit message claims 'Proven by mutation ... an unmarked copy appended to _store/hlc.py fails the guard; the same copy with a reasoned marker passes; the same copy with a bare reasonless marker fails again' — but this proof is described in prose only and is not encoded in any test in the diff.

Because the owner is skipped by name (`if rel == _OWNER: continue`, line 267) it is not the code path that establishes the excusal machinery works; the `excused` branch (lines 275-283) never runs against real input.
advisory.finding: The guard's offender-detection and escape-marker logic (`_replacement_walk_offenders`) is never exercised against a known offender: it is only called with the expectation that it returns `[]`, so the per-line atom scan, the reasoned-marker excusal branch, and the `excused=True` path are dead in the test suite. A behavior-changing regression in the guard itself (an inverted `all()`/`any()` condition, a broken marker check that always excuses, or an rglob that skips files) would leave `test_the_replacement_link_walk_has_exactly_one_body` green while the guard silently stops detecting a fourth copy — exactly the failure the epic exists to end.
scenarios: A future refactor inverts the conjunction condition (`if not all(...)` → `if any(...)`) or breaks the marker check so every file is excused; the offenders list is always empty and the test stays green, so a re-introduced fourth walker merges undetected.
The escape-marker convention is changed or the regex group index shifts; excusal silently accepts a bare marker, and no test catches it because the excusal path is never driven.
advisory.suggested_fix: Refactor the scanning core to accept an iterable of (rel_path, text) pairs so it can be unit-tested directly, then add cases asserting: an unmarked copy containing both atoms is returned as an offender; the same text with a reasoned marker on an atom line is excused; the same text with a bare `# replacement-walk-ok:` marker is still an offender.

evidence: 271:        except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - unreadable file is not a duplication signal

ABSENCE: no assertion that every discovered .py file was actually read; a decode/permission failure removes a file from consideration without surfacing it, so 'checked and clean' cannot be distinguished from 'check never ran on this file'.
dropped.finding: The offender scan silently skips any src file that raises OSError on read_text (including a UnicodeDecodeError on a genuine but non-UTF-8 .py file), so a fourth walk living in an unreadable/undecodable file is treated as 'no offender' rather than as an error — the guard's clean verdict is indistinguishable from 'this file was never actually scanned'.
dropped.suggested_fix: Collect unreadable paths and assert the list is empty, or re-raise the OSError, rather than continuing past it silently.
